text:
Maria (Sales): FYI — ACME wants to pilot a new model variant for their search-product POC. They named it Orion-XL-13B-q4. Need fit checks, pricing, and security signoff. POC kickoff next Wed.
Devon (SE): Thanks. Do we have the model artifact they want to use (HF/ggml/custom)?
Maria (Sales): Customer says HF repo + a patched tokenizer. Link: https://huggingface.co/acme/orion-xl-13b-q4 (they attached zip).
Rafi (MLOps): Quick checklist: model format (pt, safetensors), tokenizer compat, kv-cache shape, seq length. If patched tokenizer, we may need a token-merging step.
Hannah (Product): Is this variant quantized to 4-bit (q4)? That affects supported backends and perf profiles.
Maria (Sales): They called it q4 in their name. Unclear if it's our q4-int8-compatible or a custom quantization. They want dedicated throughput SLA during POC.
Devon (SE): Can someone from ML run a local load test on our staging runtime? I can stand up the POC config but need model compatibility report.
Rafi (MLOps): I pulled the artifact — it's safetensors; tokenizer is custom with extra special tokens. Model uses q4_k_m quantization (not identical to our q4kit). I ran `scripts/inspect_model.sh` and saw attention config: multihead dim mismatch warning but still loads.
Devon (SE): That mismatch worries me for kernel selection. If attention dims don't match expected layout we may need a converter or custom kernel. How big is the KV cache per token?
Rafi (MLOps): Measured ~1.1MB per token for the 13B variant in current layout. With q4_k_m it's ~0.3x the float baseline. On A100 40GB we can host one replica with room for batching. On H100 should be fine for more concurrency.
Anya (Security): Security questionnaire note: they require KMS integration, audit logs, and ephemeral storage for the model. Also want to know if the model has any trojan/backdoor scanning done. Have we run a model-scan?
Hannah (Product): We have a lightweight model-scan tool (toxins + data-leak heuristics). Rafi — can you run it and post results before EOD tomorrow?
Rafi (MLOps): Running now. Found several tokens in the custom tokenizer that map to user-supplied prompt delimiters. No obvious PII exfil patterns on synthetic tests, but need longer prompt evals.
Maria (Sales): ACME's legal also asked about pricing: POC pricing for Dedicated: how do we quote a 2-week reserved capacity with 8k qps budget? They want a flat POC fee + usage overage.
Devon (SE): For a 13B q4 on Dedicated with 1 replica on A100, estimate 200 reqs/sec under small prompts. For 8k qps they need multiple replicas (≈40). That's expensive; offer a scaled-down perf target or burst capacity.
Hannah (Product): Suggest we propose a staged POC: week 1 functional + integration (1-2 replicas), week 2 load validation with scheduled burst windows and our price cap. Provide a per-replica day rate + burst add-on. Also mention Optimize recommendations (batching, cache).
Maria (Sales): I'll draft a pricing sketch. Need definitive numbers from infra. Rafi, can you give per-replica cost estimate (A100) plus an H100 option?
Rafi (MLOps): Per-replica hourly infra cost estimate: A100: $7.50/hr, H100: $12.50/hr (includes network & storage). For 2-week POC with 3 replicas baseline + occasional bursts to 40 for tests, ballpark infra = $7k (A100) / $11k (H100). Add managed support + SRE for the POC: ~$4k.
Anya (Security): On the security questionnaire items: KMS yes via customer-managed keys in our Private offering. Audit logs: available at 30d retention by default, can extend. Ephemeral: model mount is read-only; we can use tmpfs for runtime KV caches and wipe on termination. Will prepare answers.
Maria (Sales): Great — ACME also flagged an enterprise blocker: their compliance team requires a signed MSA with SOC2 + a 3rd-party vulnerability scan. They want results before GA.
Hannah (Product): We can provide SOC2 cert and a pen-test report, but third-party model scanning is not in standard pack. Offer a one-time scan add-on and an extended SLA for the POC.
Devon (SE): Operational ask: customer uses a patched tokenizer; if we mount it at runtime we must ensure we don't allow remote code execution. Use a sanitizer: `python -m tokenizers normalize` in sandbox. Rafi, can we run tokenizer repo through the sandbox?
Rafi (MLOps): Yes — I'll run it in the sandbox image and produce a small compatibility patch if needed. If conversion required, I'll produce a `manifest.json` with fields: `model_format`, `tokenizer_patch`, `kv_cache_shape`, `quant_profile`.
Maria (Sales): Timeline: security answers and scan by EOD Fri, compatibility report Mon, POC config and estimate Tue, kickoff Wed. ACME expects that schedule. Can we meet it?
Anya (Security): EOD Fri for preliminary answers ok. Third-party scan may take 3-5 days; we can fast-track for an extra fee.
Rafi (MLOps): Compatibility report Monday looks doable — will include perf estimates for A100/H100 and a quick conversion script if needed.
Devon (SE): I'll prepare a POC playbook with step-by-step: ingest artifact -> run scanner -> deploy on staging -> run smoke tests -> load tests. Will add rollback and fallback to smaller model variant if issues.
Maria (Sales): ACME asked about fallback to a smaller model (Orion-7B) for cost. Are the outputs consistent enough to compare?
Hannah (Product): We should run a small eval set and compute embedding cosine/ROUGE/qualitative examples. Recommend adding that to acceptance criteria for POC.
deploy-bot: Ticket #IN-4742 created for "ACME Orion-XL-13B onboarding" assigned to MLOps. Link: https://redwood/infra/tickets/IN-4742
Maria (Sales): Perfect. I'll send the proposed POC outline and pricing sketch to the customer tonight. Thanks everyone — ping me if blockers pop up. :pray:
